Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> be irreducible schemes
locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0004>. Let <MATH_0005> and <MATH_0006>
be the generic points. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> are <MATH_0009>-birational,
<STRUCT_0003> there exist nonempty opens of <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011>
which are <MATH_0012>-isomorphic, and
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014> map to the same point <MATH_0015> of <MATH_0016> and
<MATH_0017> and <MATH_0018> are isomorphic as
<MATH_0019>-algebras.
<STRUCT_0005>

We have seen the equivalence of (1) and (2) in
Lemma <REF_0001>.
It is immediate that (2) implies (3).
To finish we assume (3) holds and we prove (1).
By Lemma <REF_0002>
there is a rational map <MATH_0001>
which sends <MATH_0002> to <MATH_0003> and induces
the given isomorphism <MATH_0004>.
Thus <MATH_0005> is a birational morphism and hence induces
an isomorphism on nonempty opens
by Lemma <REF_0003>.
This finishes the proof.

The following are equivalent

<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> are <MATH_0009>-birational,
<STRUCT_0003> there exist nonempty opens of <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> which are <MATH_0012>-isomorphic, and
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014> map to the same point <MATH_0015> and
<MATH_0016> as <MATH_0017>-extensions.
<STRUCT_0005>
